Title: Durrence's Pinewood Faces New Challenge
Subtitle: The Savannah Morning News private-school basketball preview included St. Andrew's boys basketball returnees for Karl Demasi's second season.
Author: C. Edward Wilson
Byline: C. Edward Wilson, Savannah Morning News
Summary: The private-school basketball preview listed Karl Demasi as St. Andrew's second-year boys basketball coach and identified Jeff Smith, Patrick Burns, and Davy Clay as key returnees after Tobi Specht and Justin Dixon graduated.
SourceCitation: C. Edward Wilson, "DURRENCE'S PINEWOOD FACES NEW CHALLENGE," Savannah Morning News (GA), November 16, 2001, Page 1C, Sports.
ArchiveNote: This archive page preserves citation details and an original summary. The full newspaper text is not republished here.
Transcript: The Savannah Morning News private-school basketball preview listed Karl Demasi as St. Andrew's second-year boys basketball coach. The preview said the Saints were coming off a 16-11 season, had lost Tobi Specht and Justin Dixon, and returned junior guard Jeff Smith, junior forward Patrick Burns, and sophomore guard Davy Clay. It described Demasi's teams as quick and tenacious defensively and said the Saints' goal was to return to the state playoffs.

Title: Memorial Day Captures Boys' Tournament Title at St. Andrew's
Subtitle: St. Andrew's fell to Memorial Day in the Holiday Invitational final.
Author: Savannah Morning News
Summary: Memorial Day beat St. Andrew's 53-46 in the Holiday Invitational championship game. Patrick Burns led the Saints with 18 points and Ben Robertson added 12.
SourceCitation: "MEMORIAL DAY CAPTURES BOYS' TOURNAMENT TITLE AT ST. ANDREW'S," Savannah Morning News (GA), December 9, 2001, Page 9C, Sports.
ArchiveNote: This archive page preserves citation details and an original summary. The full newspaper text is not republished here.
Transcript: The archive summary records St. Andrew's 53-46 Holiday Invitational final loss to Memorial Day. Burns scored 18, Robertson 12, Cam Aldrich 7, Jeff Smith 6, Davy Clay 2, and Quint Dixon 1.

Title: Final 2001-02 Prep Basketball Statistics
Subtitle: Patrick Burns, Cam Aldrich, Davy Clay, and Jeff Smith appeared on the final regular-season leaderboards.
Author: Savannah Morning News
Summary: The final regular-season statistics listed Patrick Burns with 418 points and 239 rebounds in 22 games, Cam Aldrich with 163 rebounds, Davy Clay with 71 assists and 110 steals, and Jeff Smith with 72 steals.
SourceCitation: "FINAL 2001-02 PREP BASKETBALL STATISTICS," Savannah Morning News (GA), February 15, 2002, Page 6B, Sports.
ArchiveNote: This archive page preserves citation details and an original summary. The full newspaper text is not republished here.
Transcript: The archive summary records the final regular-season statistical leaders for St. Andrew's: Burns averaged 19.0 points and 10.9 rebounds, Aldrich averaged 8.2 rebounds, Clay averaged 3.4 assists and 5.2 steals, and Jeff Smith averaged 3.3 steals.

Title: Loss to Colleton Prep Ends Saints' Season
Subtitle: St. Andrew's boys basketball season ended in the SCISA Region 4-AA Tournament.
Author: Savannah Morning News
Summary: Colleton Prep beat St. Andrew's 66-61 in the SCISA Region 4-AA Tournament. Patrick Burns scored 28, Jeff Smith had 14 points and 10 steals, and the Saints finished 16-7.
SourceCitation: "LOSS TO COLLETON PREP ENDS SAINTS' SEASON," Savannah Morning News (GA), February 20, 2002, Page 6D, Sports.
ArchiveNote: This archive page preserves citation details and an original summary. The full newspaper text is not republished here.
Transcript: The archive summary records St. Andrew's season-ending 66-61 region-tournament loss to Colleton Prep. Burns scored 28, Jeff Smith added 14 with 10 steals, Matt Hunt and Cam Aldrich scored 8 each, and Ben Robertson scored 3.

Title: Savannah Morning News All-Coastal Empire Boys Basketball Teams
Subtitle: Patrick Burns earned third-team All-Coastal Empire honors after a junior season of 14 straight double-doubles.
Author: Savannah Morning News
Summary: Patrick Burns was named to the boys All-Coastal Empire third team. The package described him as a consistent junior who posted 14 straight double-doubles and finished the season averaging 19.1 points and 10.7 rebounds.
SourceCitation: "SAVANNAH MORNING NEWS ALL-COASTAL EMPIRE," Savannah Morning News (GA), March 19, 2002, Page 4D, Sports.
ArchiveNote: This archive page preserves citation details and an original summary. The full newspaper text is not republished here.
Transcript: The Savannah Morning News boys All-Coastal Empire basketball package named Patrick Burns to the third team. Burns was listed as a 6-foot-1, 170-pound junior forward from St. Andrew's who had 14 straight double-doubles and averaged 19.1 points and 10.7 rebounds.
